scope: Self-test fixture: narration of the fixture scripts and the fixture panels.
note: The governance story lands its owners and its score, and the stewardship loop closes on a named human. What it does not yet do is tie lot traceability to the regulation that demands it. Fix that before this goes outside the company.

verdicts.evidence: The data products list shows Supply Chain Health and Last Mile Performance with their owners, active in the marketplace.
Supply Chain Health is a data product: owned by Henrik Jansen, with a schema, a refresh every fifteen minutes and a trust score target of zero point eight five.
The trust score is computed by the platform from validity, completeness, discoverability and usage, and recalculated as the data changes.
eight thousand two hundred products with no weight on file, and six hundred and forty addresses we could not resolve
A human steward fixes them, and the correction flows back into the pipeline.
A Data Quality Agent turns "every perishable item must have a lot number" into a rule and shows you the violations.
verdicts.gap: Said only in the AI video; the governance video never shows a rule being written from a business statement.

verdicts.evidence: Every gold field traces back through silver and bronze to the source system, and impact analysis tells you which apps you are about to break.
Twenty-five business terms are governed in the glossary, each linked to the dataset that computes it.

verdicts.gap: Neither EC 178/2002 nor the NVWA citation is mentioned, so lot traceability reads as housekeeping rather than a regulatory obligation.

verdicts.evidence: It is shareable over an API and discoverable in the marketplace.
